meta.title: CyberWithMadhav Terminal Wargame: 20 levels of Linux basics (inspired by OverTheWire Bandit, original content)

fs_schema.root: Each level.fs is the root directory node (name '/'). Node fields: type ('dir' or 'file'), name, owner, group, perms (9 char symbolic string such as 'rw-r-----'; 't' in the last slot means sticky and counts as x), size (bytes; files: always equals content length, dirs: 4096), content (files only, string; may contain control characters for binary looking files), children (dirs only, array of nodes).

extra_root_keys.user: login name of the player for this level (cadetNN)
extra_root_keys.groups: array of {name, gid}; the first entry is the primary group; used by id and by permission checks
extra_root_keys.history: optional array of earlier commands, oldest first; history prints these then the commands typed this session

fs_schema.permission_model: Pick the owner triplet if node.owner equals user, else the group triplet if node.group is in the player groups, else the other triplet. Reading a file needs r; listing a dir needs r; entering or passing through a dir needs x on every directory in the path. The player is never root.
fs_schema.paths: Absolute, relative, '.', '..' and '~' are supported. A lone '-' given to cat means standard input, which is empty in this game.

shell: pipes with | (every stage must be an allowed command)
wildcards * and ? in the last path part of unquoted words (hidden names only match if the pattern starts with a dot)
2>/dev/null to hide error output of a command
head: -n N
-nN
-N
default 10
file: one or more paths; prints 'ASCII text', 'data', 'empty', 'directory' or 'regular file, no read permission'
find: prints Permission denied for unreadable dirs on stderr
grep: PATTERN (treat as a regular expression; all levels use plain literals)
uniq: -c (count right aligned in 7 columns then a space)
strings: printable runs are ASCII 0x20 to 0x7e plus tab
base64 -d: file or stdin; whitespace and line breaks ignored; encoding is not needed
chmod: symbolic u, g, o, a with +, = or minus and r, w, x, comma separated
only the owner may chmod; otherwise 'Operation not permitted'

notes: Every password is a random 32 character alphanumeric string generated with Python secrets.

Levels lvl10, lvl17 and lvl19 store the password base64 encoded on purpose, so it appears literally only after decoding; every other level stores it in plain text. The checker confirmed each password lives in exactly one file of its level, raw or decoded.
Some levels also verify that the naive approach fails (for example cat with a lone dash, unquoted names with spaces, grep without the ignore case flag, cat before chmod).
Solutions are one valid path; the JS engine should check the password the player submits, not the exact commands typed.
Content is original and only inspired by the format of OverTheWire Bandit. No real system is touched; everything runs in the browser.
sort uses plain byte order (no locale), which matches the default JS string sort for ASCII text.
Passwords are not stored in this file in plain form. Each level keeps password_sha256, the SHA-256 hex digest of the password that unlocks the next level; the game compares hashes.
Level fs trees are kept exactly as authored.

levels.goal: The password for the next level is stored in a file called readme in your home directory. Read it.
